newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 10.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Monday:

* The Clinton Administration wants to accelerate the nation's change to digital, high-definition television programming in order to speed up the auction of newly vacated channels, a move that would help the Federal Budget by generating an estimated $15 million in auction proceeds.

* The latest Nielsen ratings show more than one million fewer homes watched television in February compared to a year earlier, marking the fourth year out of five in which overall prime-time viewing has declined. Television industry executives challenge such figures and have united to support an experimental rival to the Nielsen rating system.
* News Analysis: On Tuesday Microsoft is to announce plans to release a test copy of the newest version of its World Wide Web browser program, the Internet Explorer.

* Films targeting young, black urban viewers are increasingly opening in mid-week to avoid the gang violence that plagued the Friday night premiers of films such as "New Jack City" and "Boyz 'N the Hood."

* Americans are relinquishing their right to sue in the wake of corporate notices detailing new arbitration requirments and recent court decisions making it easier for companies to demand that claims be handled out of court.
* The U.S. Congress has begun debating the role of Government in regulating health care and seems likely to set standards for health maintenance organizations.

* Some former stockholders of the Providence Journal-Bulletin and its parent company are questioning the loss of the paper's independence after last month's sale of the Providence Journal Co to A.H. Belo for $1.5 billion.

* Established media companies are teaming with popular World Wide Web sites to expand their audiences, as shown by the recent partnership between CBS and Sportsline USA and possible talks between ABC and Starwave.

* Some believe Lucent Technologies could make an acquisition to become a stronger force in data networking. Names mentioned are Ascend Communications, Fore Systems, Bay Networks and Cascade Communications.
* Some efforts to create new area codes for telephone numbers are meeting resistance.
* Miller Brewing Co, a unit of Philip Morris, and the Fallon McElligott agency are defending the new advertisements for Miller Lite beer based on the work of a fictitious character named Dick.
* Netscape Communications is expected to announce on Monday its third generation of software to compete with Microsoft and appeal to businesses.
* Companies such as IBM are offering sites on the World Wide Web where browsers can look up the archived abstracts for patents issued by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.
